content: Once upon a time, I dreamed I was a butterfly, fluttering hither and thither, to all intents and purposes a butterfly. Suddenly I awoke, and there I was, unmistakably Zhuangzi. But I do not know whether I was then a man dreaming I was a butterfly, or whether I am now a butterfly, dreaming I am a man.
author: Zhuangzi
sourceWork: The Book of Zhuangzi, Chapter 2 (On the Equality of Things)
explanation: Zhuangzi's iconic parable shatters rigid boundaries between subjective ego and objective reality. By questioning whether waking life is itself a form of cosmic dreaming, he invites us to release dogmatic certainty and embrace the fluid mystery of existence.
practicalInsight: When today's problems feel overwhelmingly heavy, remind yourself of the dreamlike, transient nature of all temporary appearances.
reflectionPrompt: What waking anxiety are you taking with absolute seriousness that might look like a fleeting dream from a higher vantage point?
